text:
BofA Securities kept its Buy rating on $TSM with a price objective of $620 per share, 55% above the $398 price at publication. 

The note focuses on Arizona: a new long-term power contract that lifts the site's electricity supply to 1.88 GW, enough in BofA's estimate to triple advanced-node capacity, and evidence that the US fabs are profitable even before government grants.

The numbers behind BofA's estimate:

- Power: TSMC and Arizona Public Service signed a long-term agreement that extends electricity service to 1.88 GW at full buildout, up from 1.2 GW. Because TSMC makes an upfront credit-support payment in January 2027, APS treats the full 1.88 GW as committed demand and could supply more. 

- Capacity: At about 10 MW per 1,000 wafers a month of advanced-node capacity, plus some power for back-end packaging, BofA estimates the site could reach ~150k wafers a month, against ~50k by Q4 2027. That is roughly three times the 2027 level. 

- Revenue: At the current build cadence this could be in place by 2035, before the additional facilities announced earlier this year, and generate more than $60bn of revenue a year. For scale, BofA expects TSMC's total revenue to be about $176bn in 2026. 

Securing power years ahead is what turns announced fabs into a buildable plan. The deal removes one of the main physical constraints on the US expansion and gives customers seeking US-made chips more visibility on supply.

- Capacity: At about 10 MW per 1,000 wafers a month of advanced-node capacity, plus some power for back-end packaging, BofA estimates the site could reach ~150k wafers a month, against ~50k by Q4 2027. That is roughly three times the 2027 level.

"In case you're wondering, what Luxor does is they make software that lets Bitcoin miners manage their machines. So it's not doing the mining, it's the software that does the management."

"It wasn't a huge amount, but again, another novel attack surface that nobody had seen coming for crypto-related software, and it becomes absolutely exhausting."

"So far this is only 0.243 Bitcoin. But if you're mining Bitcoin or looking at Bitcoin miners or using software that's related to it, now you have to be worried about that as well."

"The miners got the electricity bill for it, but the hacker got the direct deposit."

It's something the board *has* to look into and potentially (that's where it's up to dispute) take action on.

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。

3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望：
近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。

(1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。

(2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。

(3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU

MSCI All Country World Index (ACWI) earnings are expected to grow +34% YoY in 2026.

The Information Technology sector is set to account for 48% of this expansion, matching the combined contribution of the next 7 sectors.

Excluding years when global EPS declined YoY, this would mark the 2nd-highest level of single-sector earnings concentration over the last 30 years, exceeded only during the 2022 energy crisis.

The AI Revolution is driving a historic surge in earnings.

en_summary: The “overhead supply wall” above SPY is probably not a wall. Nearly half of SPY’s volume since June...
text:
🚨 THE “OVERHEAD SUPPLY WALL” ABOVE SPY IS PROBABLY NOT A WALL.

Nearly half of SPY’s volume since July traded between 761 and 773.

SPY closed Friday at 754.37.

The busiest price was 767, leaving a massive block of supposedly trapped investors above the market.

The conventional argument is simple:

Those investors will sell when SPY returns to breakeven, creating resistance and capping any rally.

It sounds logical.

The data does not support it.

We preregistered the test, built point-in-time volume profiles and studied SPY, QQQ, IWM and DIA back to 2016.

If overhead supply actually suppresses price, larger overhead volume should predict less upside.

It predicted the opposite.

Across the four index ETFs, heavier overhead supply was associated with greater 10-session upside, not less.

The result remained positive across 20, 60 and 120-session volume profiles and in both halves of the sample.

Then we isolated 24 comparable SPY setups.

Over the following 20 sessions:

Average return: +1.80%

Median return: +3.17%

Positive outcomes: 67%

Reached the overhead volume shelf: 67%

But here is the important part.

Comparable SPY pullbacks reached any price the same distance above the market roughly 76% of the time.

The volume shelf was not a special magnet.

It was not a reliable ceiling either.

It was simply another price.

This is not a buy signal. The sample is small, and the outcomes varied widely.

It is the removal of a sell signal.

The current 767 shelf is only 1.7

Let’s take this gentleman’s argument at face value that anyone can throw money at rockets and get something like Starship, Falcon or Dragon.

Perhaps he can explain to everyone how SpaceX is able to catch giant starships from orbit with chopsticks and deliver 85% of all Earth payload to orbit with Falcon, while Blue Origin, which started before SpaceX and was funded by the immensely wealthy Jeff Bezos, is not yet able to launch reliably?

Also, why is it that Boeing and Lockheed received several times what SpaceX did from the government for development of their rockets and spacecraft, but the Boeing capsule is still not operational and ULA delivers less than 5% of SpaceX payload to orbit?

I am genuinely curious about these questions.
